outcome: maternal anxiety (Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale - APAIS)
cohort: The study included 51 obstetric patients aged 20-40 years, classified as American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) groups 1 or 2, who were scheduled for elective caesarean surgery for their first baby.
finding: Midazolam premedication (0.03 mg/kg) significantly decreased maternal anxiety without adversely affecting the newborn's Apgar score.
mod_finding: Midazolam premedication prior to elective caesarean section was effective in reducing maternal anxiety without significantly impacting the Apgar scores of babies born via caesarean.
